reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first two premises by showing that pre-strained 22K steel retains hydrogen after air exposure while un-prestrained steel releases it, and that fracture energy decreases with hydrogen and pre-strain. However, it provides no data on oxide layer degradation or corrosion, leaving the remaining premises unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Pre-strain introduces dislocation trapping sites that retain hydrogen in steel.
Hydrogen retention in pre-strained steel persists after air exposure, while un-prestrained steel releases almost all hydrogen.
Retained hydrogen degrades the passive oxide layer.
Degraded oxide layer promotes localized corrosion and embrittlement.
Un-prestrained steel with hydrogen out-diffusion maintains a robust passive oxide film and corrosion resistance.
